Use users as bootstrap clusters: retain all overlapping prefixes, perturbation repeats, and paired baseline/perturbed outcomes together. For an equal-user estimand, average paired differences across repeats within each prefix, then prefixes within each user; average user effects within each category. Resample users with replacement within each category, preserving pairing; recompute the four-category macro mean in every replicate. Obtain a 95% percentile interval from the replicate macro means’ 2.5th/97.5th percentiles; do not average category interval endpoints. If identifiable users span categories, resample their complete cross-category records jointly. This applies the principle that resampling must preserve within-subject dependence and reflect sampling design. Report unique-user counts and clarify that intervals condition on the fitted models and audit protocol. [Cluster-bootstrap methodology](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7148287/)

Without reliable user IDs, user-clustered confidence intervals are unavailable: sequence hashes cannot reliably join overlapping prefixes or distinguish users with identical histories. Defensible reporting is descriptive paired effects, empirical quantiles, observed row/prefix counts, and explicitly conditional variability across perturbation seeds—not population confidence intervals or independent-user sample sizes. Recommended implementation: construct a seeded audit sample from public user histories when available; otherwise label it a row sample. Prespecify caps on users/category, prefixes/user, perturbation types and repeats; document truncation. Sampling and repeat counts explicitly trade computation against precision. Cache baseline outputs, batch perturbations under inference mode, and bootstrap cached scalar outcomes without rerunning inference. With C categories, U users/category, P prefixes/user, K perturbations and R repeats, cap sequence evaluations at C×U×P×(1+K×R); separately report candidate/catalog scoring cost, measured GPU time and peak memory before claiming inexpensive execution. [Sampling/repeat controls](https://scikit-learn.org/1.4/modules/generated/sklearn.inspection.permutation_importance.html)
